answers.d01: 似然回答的是：固定手头的数据，哪个假设最能让这批数据出现？先分清方向。已知硬币公平，问十次全正的概率，那是 P(数据|假设) = 0.5¹⁰ ≈ 0.001。似然反过来：你不知道硬币是否公平，只看到十次全正，于是比较各假设「生产」这批数据的能力——公平硬币产出它的可能性 0.001，十次全正的硬币产出 1。同一批数据对不同假设各有一个似然值，比大小才有意义。注意似然不是「该假设为真的概率」：各假设的似然加起来不必等于 1，它只衡量数据的支持面。要变成「看完数据后假设为真的概率」（后验），需用贝叶斯公式乘上先验：后验 ∝ 似然 × 先验。若你事先九成相信硬币公平，十次全正会把这份信心拉低。数据相同、先验不同，后验就不同——这正是似然与后验的分界。
answers.d02: Variance measures spread around the average. Two classes can both average 70: one scoring 69, 70, 71; another 40, 70, 100. The mean hides that difference; variance captures it. For a whole population: subtract the mean from each value, square each gap, average the squares. Class B: gaps −30, 0, +30, squares 900, 0, 900, variance 600; Class A is about 0.67. Squaring does two jobs: raw gaps cancel to zero (−30+0+30=0), and merely removing signs would count a 30-point miss the same as a 10-point miss—squaring makes big misses dominate. The price is squared units, so people often report the square root (standard deviation, about 24.5 here) to speak in points again. Same average, different spread—variance is the number that tells them apart, and tightening 40–100 to 60–80 at the same mean drops it from 600 to about 67.
answers.d03: 正反馈是「结果反过来加强原因」的回路：变化发生后被送回起点，推动同一方向继续变。麦克风对准音箱就会啸叫——话筒拾到音箱的声音，放大播出，又被拾到，一圈比一圈响。冰面融化同理：变暖使冰化，深色海水比冰吸收更多阳光，于是更暖、化得更快。放大的条件是每绕一圈至少把变化原样甚至加倍送回；一旦出现饱和或消耗（音量到顶、冰全化完），增长就停。但它不等于「好」：放大只描述方向，不描述评价。存款复利、产品口碑都是正反馈，让人受益；恐慌挤兑、啸叫则有害。同一个结构既可成就也可毁掉，判断好坏要看它放大的是什么。
answers.d04: Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up when choosing one thing—only the single best one, not everything you could have done. A free afternoon with three options: study for Monday's exam, meet a friend, nap. You choose the friend. The cost isn't 'exam plus nap'; it's whichever you'd have picked instead—say, studying. That lost prep time is the real price of the outing, though no money changed hands. Two habits follow. Count what you skip, not just what you pay: a 'free' concert still costs the afternoon. And compare honestly, because rankings can flip—if the exam decides your grade, skipping it costs too much; if you're exhausted, the forgone nap is the true cost. Change one condition and the answer moves: push the exam to next month and the afternoon gets cheap, showing that the cost lives in the alternative you'd actually have taken.
answers.d05: 某病发病率 1%。检测很准：病人 99% 呈阳性，健康人 5% 误报阳性。你检出阳性，真患病的概率是多少？多数人猜 99%，实际约 16.7%。想象 10000 人：患病 100 人中 99 人阳性；健康 9900 人中 5% = 495 人误报。阳性共 594 人，真病人只占 99/594 ≈ 16.7%。写成公式：P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病) / P(阳性) = 0.99×0.01 / 0.594。分母把所有通向阳性的路加起来——真病人加上被误报的健康人。关键是分清两个方向：说明书上的 99% 是 P(阳性|患病)，即「有病的人多容易显阳性」；你要的是反过来的 P(患病|阳性)，两者隔着发病率。发病率升到 10%，同样的检测下，阳性者患病概率就升到约 68.8%——先验变了，结论跟着变。
answers.d06: Cache invalidation is deciding when a cached copy is too old to serve. A web app keeps a user's profile in memory so page views skip the database—fast, until the user changes their avatar. The database now has the new photo, the cache still holds the old one, and visitors keep seeing it until something retires that entry. Retiring it is invalidation. Caching is easy; knowing when is hard. Common choices: expire after a fixed time (simple, but stale in the meantime), delete the entry whenever the data is written (fresh, but every write must reach the cache too), or bake a version into the key so new data lands under a new name and the old copy expires harmlessly. The rule of thumb: the more a value can change unnoticed, the more invalidation costs—for a bank balance you'd invalidate on every write, or not cache at all.
answers.d07: 冰淇淋销量和溺水人数同涨同跌，相关很强，但冰淇淋不会让人溺水——背后是同一个隐藏因素：夏天。天热让两件事都变多，这叫混杂。单看数据，分不清是 A 导致 B、B 导致 A、还是 C 同时推动两者，甚至纯属巧合；相关只说明「知道一个能更好地猜另一个」，不说明改动一个会改变另一个。区分的办法是走出单纯观察：做对照实验，随机让一半人吃冰淇淋、一半不吃，若溺水率仍同步变化，因果才立得住——随机化让「夏天」这类混杂在两组里均摊掉。做不了实验时退而求其次：只比较同样温度的日子（控制混杂），核对时序（原因须在前），追问机制（糖分和水流之间讲不出通路）。再换个条件检验：只在冬季数据里看，这条相关基本消失——说明原相关主要由夏天的混杂撑着，而非两者直接相连。
answers.d08: Compound growth adds each period's gain to the base, so gains earn gains: an amount P grows to P(1+r)ⁿ. At 10% a year, 10,000 becomes 11,000, then 12,100, then 13,310—the yearly gain itself grows from 1,000 to 1,100, because last year's extra 100 now earns too. After 30 years you have about 174,500, not the 40,000 simple interest would give. The starting amount matters because growth is multiplicative: it scales whatever you begin with. 100,000 and 10,000 both grow about 17-fold in those 30 years—1.75 million versus 174,500—and the gap never narrows on its own; same rate, same time, proportions preserved. Two other levers bite hard: at 7% instead of 10%, that 10,000 reaches only about 76,000; and because gains feed on earlier gains, the final decade adds more than the first—starting ten years later leaves you with about 40% of the final amount. The model assumes a steady rate; real returns fluctuate and fees cut in.
answers.v01: 过拟合是「把旧题背下来了，却没学到解法」。设想你根据过去三年的餐厅流水预测未来，数据里有个巧合：每逢周二下雨生意就差。若这是真规律，预测会准；若只是巧合，你就把噪音当成了信号——模型在旧数据上近乎全对，换到新数据立刻失灵，这就是过拟合。所以判断不能只看它在学过的数据上的成绩，要留一部分数据不给它看：旧数据漂亮、新数据明显变差，就是信号。对策也顺着这个思路：规律越简单越背不动题，数据越多巧合越难成立。条件变了结论也变：若未来与过去完全同类，背题无利可图；现实总在变，所以适度「钝」的模型往往走得更远。
answers.v02: Search your notes for 'cache' and get 10 results: 6 truly about caching, 4 hits on the word 'catching'. Precision asks: of what I showed you, how much was right? 6/10 = 60%. It protects you from junk. Recall asks: of everything relevant, how much did I find? If your notes hold 20 relevant items, you got 6/20 = 30%. It protects you from missing things. The two pull against each other: return only the top hit and precision may be 100% while recall falls to 5%; return every document and recall is 100%, drowned in noise. Which to favor depends on the cost of each error: medical screening tolerates false alarms to avoid missing cases (recall first); a search engine tolerates misses rather than flooding you (precision first).
answers.v03: 把自然选择讲成「生物为了适应而努力，努力被遗传」是常见误读。真正的机制不需要任何意图，只需三件事叠加：个体之间存在差异（有的跑得快，有的慢）；差异能遗传（快的后代多半也快）；资源有限，慢的留下更少后代。结果是「快」在下一代中的占比上升——被选择的是已存在的差异，不是个体的意愿。长颈鹿不是把脖子伸长才传给后代，而是祖先里脖子上限本来有高有低，够得着高处的留下更多后代，许多代后种群里长脖子的比例变高；任何一只动物的一生都不会因此改写基因。条件一变，方向就变：天敌消失后，「快」不再多留后代，还可能因维持成本被淘汰；迁入新环境，原本中性的特征可能变成优势。选择改变的是种群的比例构成，不是个体的主动改造。
answers.v04: Idempotent: doing it twice has the same effect as doing it once. You need it because distributed systems retry. You POST 'charge $100', the network times out, and you can't tell whether it went through—so the client resends. If charging isn't idempotent, the customer pays twice. The fix is making repetition harmless. Patterns: attach a client-generated idempotency key, and the server remembers processed keys, returning the stored result instead of charging again; use conditional writes ('set status to shipped if it is paid'), so a retry finds the condition already met and does nothing; or phrase the operation as an absolute value rather than a delta ('set cart quantity to 3', not 'add 1'). That contrast is the core: 'add 1' is not idempotent, 'set to 1' is. Treat every request as possibly delivered twice, and build idempotency in before the first retry happens.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量「结果揭晓前你有多悬」。掷一枚均匀硬币，正反各半，最难猜；一枚两面皆正的硬币，毫无悬念。熵把这种悬念变成数字，常用 H = −Σ p·log₂p。均匀硬币：H = 1 比特；正面占 0.99 的硬币：H ≈ 0.08 比特；完全确定则熵为 0。为什么均匀最不确定？因为此时每种结果都「有戏」，你没有任何可压的优势；只要概率偏向某一边，你就多少能猜得更准，悬念随之减少。对数的作用是让独立事件的不确定性可以相加，其推论是：总概率为 1 时，平摊概率使熵最大。换条件验证：六面均匀骰子的熵升到 log₂6 ≈ 2.58 比特——选项更多且同样均匀，悬念更大；骰子被灌铅到几乎总出六点，熵又掉回近 0。熵只看概率分布，不问结果好坏。
answers.v06: Deadlock: a group of processes each hold some resources and each wait for a resource another member holds, so none can ever proceed. Two processes, one printer and one file lock. A grabs the printer, then asks for the file lock; B grabs the file lock, then asks for the printer. Each holds one and waits for the other's, and neither releases until it gets the rest—so both wait forever. Four conditions must all hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion (resources can't be shared), hold-and-wait (keeping one while requesting another), no preemption (you can't forcibly take a resource back), and circular wait (A waits for B, B waits for A). Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible—that's the practical toolkit: acquire all resources up front (kills hold-and-wait), or impose a global order where everyone must request the file lock before the printer (kills the circle). If B releases the file lock before asking for the printer, the deadlock disappears too.
answers.v07: 公共物品有两个特征：不排他（没法把不付钱的人挡在外面）和不竞争（多一人使用不减少别人的量）。路灯、国防、清洁的空气都是——你付不付钱，灯都照着你。这直接催生搭便车：既然不掏钱也享受得到，理性的选择就是等别人出钱。每个人都这么想，路灯就没人建，明明对大家值钱的东西却供给不足。一栋楼五户，装门禁灯花 5000 元，每户觉得值 1500 元：对社会划算（总价值 7500 超过成本），但每户都盼别家先掏，往往装不成。条件一变结论就变：一旦能排他（收费才能进的公园），或人数少到能当面分摊、互相盯梢，搭便车的空间就缩小，私人供给变得可行。政府用税收强制出资、给专利设时限换公开，都是在补这个缺口。
answers.v08: Little's law: in a stable system, L = λW — average number of items in the system equals arrival rate times average time each spends there. Coffee shop: 10 customers arrive per minute, each spends 3 minutes inside; then on average 30 people are in the shop at any moment. Count heads or compute it—the two agree, regardless of arrival pattern, service-time variation, or queue discipline. It's a bookkeeping identity, not a claim about any individual customer. The catch is stability: arrivals and service must balance so the line doesn't grow without bound. At 20 arrivals per minute with service still averaging 3 minutes, the shop fills forever and no steady-state L exists. In practice, measure any two quantities to get the third: a server taking 100 requests per second with 200 in flight has average latency W = L/λ = 2 seconds; halve the latency and the in-flight count halves too.
